facts.label: legend
facts.quote: The hill has a Hanuman temple at the top. It has about 575 steps. The temple has a rock-carved idol of Lord Hanuman.
facts.text: Local pilgrimage tradition at Anegundi near Hampi designates the 575-step Anjeyanadri hillock as the physical birthplace of Hanuman.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Traditionally known as Pampakshetra of Kishkindha, Hampi is situated on the southern bank of the river Tungabhadra. The monuments of Vijayanagara city... were built between AD 1336-1570
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India notes that Hampi, traditionally venerated as Pampa Kshetra in Kishkindha, features historical monuments constructed between 1336 CE and 1570 CE.

facts.label: scripture
facts.quote: For geographical validation, the committee turned to the Skanda Purana, where Sage Matanga tells Hanuman's mother Anjani Devi that Venkatachalam is to the north of Swarnamukhi river and located at a distance of 12 yojanas from Ahobilam
facts.text: The TTD study highlighted passages from the Skanda Purana locating Anjana's penance at Venkatachalam exactly 12 yojanas from Ahobilam.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: TTD's claim has created a stir in religious, archaeological, and political circles in Karnataka because Hampi near Ballari is considered 'Kishkindha Kshetra' or monkey kingdom for ages
facts.text: Following TTD's announcement in 2021, historians and religious organizations in Karnataka disputed the claim, arguing that historical geography and epic traditions identify Kishkindha around Hampi.

facts.label: legend
facts.quote: In some of the Puranas it is relayed that Hanuman's mother, Anjana Devi... resolved to undertake strict penance in the hills near her father's hermitage.
facts.text: Oral folklore in Maharashtra identifies the 1300-metre-high Anjaneri hill near Trimbakeshwar as the birthplace where Anjana performed penance after receiving a curse.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: This temple was probably erected during the supremacy of the local Yadava rulers during 850 AD to 1060 AD.
facts.source_name: Archaeological Survey of India, Aurangabad Circle
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India has documented ancient stone temples at Anjaneri constructed during the regional reign of the Seuna Yadava dynasty starting around 850 CE.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Jain temple in the vicinity of Anjaneri village has an inscription of Yadava or Seuna Monarch Seunadeva. He is represented to have made an endowment to Chandraprabhu Jain temple at Anjaneri in Saka Year 1063 or 1141 AD.
facts.text: A stone inscription dated to 1141 CE at Anjaneri records an endowment by the Yadava feudatory Mahasamanta Seunadeva to a local shrine, establishing medieval royal patronage of the hill complex.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: TTD's claim has created a stir in religious, archaeological, and political circles in Karnataka because Hampi near Ballari is considered 'Kishkindha Kshetra' or monkey kingdom for ages
facts.text: Historians dispute whether the poetic toponym Kishkindha in the Valmiki Ramayana refers to modern Hampi or reflects an indeterminate legendary landscape that cannot be mapped exclusively to one contemporary site.
